dual_implementation_finding.headline: The repository contains TWO divergent, unreconciled World Model implementations, and neither is currently wired into a working, checkpoint-backed demo.

track_a_audited.name: Audited research track (Phases 3.5-9I)
track_a_audited.architecture: d_model=128, heads=4, layers=2, input=[6,157] from data/windows/*.csv via world_model_dataset.py
track_a_audited.status: Rigorously trained, evaluated under a shared fair protocol (Phase 8A), leakage-audited (Phase 3.5/world_model_dataset.validate_world_model_samples), calibration-audited (Phase 8B), explainability-audited (Phase 7C), MITRE-stage-audited (Phase 7B). Real checkpoints exist (experiments/results/phase6b_vector_world_model*/model/best_model.pt, confirmed present).
track_a_audited.gap: Never imported or called by any Django-reachable code path (confirmed by repo-wide grep for VectorWorldModel: 16 hits, all under experiments/). It is not the model behind any live demo.

track_b_unaudited.name: Unaudited demo track
track_b_unaudited.architecture: state_dim=128, heads=8, layers=4, sequence_length=20, forecast_horizon=5, native per-step attack_probs AND mitre_logits outputs -- architecturally capable of per-step forecasting, which Track A is not
track_b_unaudited.status: Backs a fully-built 5-tab Streamlit dashboard (world_model/src/streamlit.py, 954 lines: Real Traffic Forecast, Benchmark, Explainability, MITRE ATT&CK, Architecture tabs) with its own feature pipeline (world_model/feature_extraction.py, reads raw CIC-IDS-2018 CSVs directly, NOT data/windows/*.csv) and its own 7-class MITRE taxonomy (world_model/config.yaml: Benign, Reconnaissance, Initial Access, Execution, Lateral Movement, Command & Control, Exfiltration).
track_b_unaudited.gap: No checkpoint exists anywhere in the repository (models/best_world_model.pth absent, confirmed by verify_repository_facts) -- the Streamlit app currently fails to load the model and shows an error. Its 'Benchmark' tab's hardcoded comparison numbers (F1=0.6941, AUC=0.8323 for 'World Model') are traced to world_model/evaluation_results.json, which used a NON-STANDARD split (files literally named Wednesday-28-INFIL-TRAIN.csv / -INFIL-TEST.csv that do not exist in data/windows/ or data/raw/ -- an ad-hoc, undocumented split of the single Infiltration day) and shows a scientifically suspicious pattern: precision=0, recall=0, F1=0 on validation at ALL 5 forecast horizons at the selected threshold, yet recall 0.79-0.85 on test -- a validation/test inversion consistent with leakage or an invalid evaluation methodology. These numbers MUST NOT be cited as evidence of anything.

dual_implementation_finding.track_b_zero_shot_note: A separate, better-designed (but still unaudited) experiment also exists: world_model/zero_shot_results.json trains on 5 attack-free-of-Infiltration days, validates on a 6th, and tests on the ENTIRE held-out Wednesday-28-02-2018 Infiltration day (a genuine leave-one-attack-family-out design). Result: validation AUC 0.9999 collapses to test AUC 0.37-0.43 (worse than random) with <1.5% recall at every horizon on the wholly unseen attack family. This is a believable, useful PRELIMINARY negative signal for unseen-attack generalization (Step 5 of this audit), but was never run through the audited/leakage-checked Phase 3.5 dataset interface, so it is cited here only as motivating evidence for a properly audited repeat experiment (see roadmap P1), never as a validated finding.
dual_implementation_finding.production_path_note: The Django dashboard (dashboard/views.py -> feature_engine.services.ingest_live_events -> run_pipeline.run_pipeline_events -> forecasting.mitre_mapping/attack_chain/victim + world_model.inference_service.AttackForecastService) is a THIRD code path, distinct from both tracks above. Its model loader (world_model/inference_service.py:92-94) looks for models/attack_forecaster.pt, which also does not exist, so it falls back to a 2-layer sigmoid heuristic (world_model/inference_service.py:13-24, 113-115) -- reporting model_source: 'heuristic_fallback'. Its MITRE/attack-chain/victim outputs come from forecasting.attack_chain.AttackChainBuilder and forecasting.victim.NextVictimForecaster, which are real, tested, production-reachable, but were DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from Phase 7D's audited MITRE trajectory narrative (experiments/tests.py: test_attack_chain_builder_never_used verifies AttackChainBuilder.predict_next_stage() is never called by the audited research scripts) -- meaning the live dashboard's stage/chain output is a separate, less-rigorously-validated heuristic than what Phases 7B/7D actually validated.
dual_implementation_finding.mitre_taxonomy_inconsistency: Three different MITRE taxonomies coexist: (1) PS requires 5 named stages (Reconnaissance, Initial Access, Lateral Movement, Command & Control, Exfiltration); (2) Phase 7B's audited 6 classes are BENIGN, CREDENTIAL_ACCESS, LATERAL_MOVEMENT, COMMAND_AND_CONTROL, IMPACT, INITIAL_ACCESS -- missing Reconnaissance and Exfiltration, includes two classes the PS doesn't name; (3) world_model/config.yaml (unaudited track) has 7 classes including Reconnaissance and Exfiltration but is untrained/unvalidated. No single audited taxonomy in this repository fully covers the PS's 5 named stages.

requirement_matrix.PS Requirement: Flow-level features (NetFlow/IPFIX): src/dst IP/port pairs, TCP flags, protocol, bytes/packets/flow, duration, IAT stats, bidirectional ratios
requirement_matrix.Exact/faithful PS interpretation: Model input should be built from these flow-level fields
requirement_matrix.Current NetOracle implementation: 157 features from CICFlowMeter-derived data/windows/*.csv (protocol, ports [dst_port__sum/mean], byte/packet counts, flow duration, IAT-style aggregates, TCP flag counts all present); raw Src/Dst IP identity is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from model features (POTENTIAL_IDENTIFIER policy, docs/CIC_IDS2018_FEATURE_POLICY.md) to avoid host-memorization shortcuts
requirement_matrix.Scientific confidence: High confidence the design choice is defensible; not a literal match to PS wording (IP identity excluded by design)
requirement_matrix.Missing work: None required for correctness; optionally document the exclusion rationale in the architecture doc for judges

requirement_matrix.PS Requirement: Packet-level features (PCAP-derived): TTL/variance, TCP window size, IP fragment flags, payload size distribution, port-scan signatures, retransmission counts
requirement_matrix.Exact/faithful PS interpretation: Model input should also incorporate packet-level signal
requirement_matrix.Current NetOracle implementation: Extraction capability DEMONSTRATED on real PCAPs (Phase 9D-9G: TTL, TCP window, IP fragmentation, payload length all confirmed DIRECT/available; retransmission and port-scan indicators explicitly classified NOT IMPLEMENTED / DERIVED-HEURISTIC, honestly). NOT integrated into the trained forecasting model: Phase 9H/9I established the only available PCAP data (449/449 per-host captures) cannot be validly paired with the flow-level CSV population (RED verdict both phases)
requirement_matrix.Scientific confidence: High confidence extraction works; high confidence current integration is NOT scientifically valid with available data
requirement_matrix.Missing work: Requires new, non-single-host PCAP data or authoritative timezone documentation before packet-level features can be legitimately integrated (see Phase 9I recommendation)

requirement_matrix.PS Requirement: Network state represented as structured feature vector OR graph encoding active flows at time t
requirement_matrix.Exact/faithful PS interpretation: Either representation is explicitly acceptable per PS wording
requirement_matrix.Current NetOracle implementation: Feature vector representation S(t) in R^157, used throughout Phases 3.5-9I. Graph representation explored and characterized (Phase 9E: sparse, host-dependent, 30.9%-80.5% non-empty windows) but not used as the production representation

requirement_matrix.PS Requirement: Learn P(S_t+1 | S_t) via sequence model (LSTM / Temporal Transformer / GNN suggested)
requirement_matrix.Exact/faithful PS interpretation: Core world-model requirement: learned state-transition dynamics
requirement_matrix.Current NetOracle implementation: VectorWorldModel's LatentTransition module: learned residual z(k+1)=z(k)+f(z(k)), applied recursively 6x, trained end-to-end with a real state-reconstruction (MSE) loss against ground-truth future states Y

requirement_matrix.PS Requirement: Generalize to unseen attack patterns, not merely memorize signatures
requirement_matrix.Exact/faithful PS interpretation: Requires an evaluation design that actually holds out an attack TYPE/family, not just a random or purely temporal split
requirement_matrix.Current NetOracle implementation: NOT tested in the audited Phase 3-9I pipeline (that pipeline uses a chronological-within-day split, not an attack-family holdout). A preliminary, UNAUDITED experiment exists (world_model/zero_shot_results.json) suggesting POOR generalization to a wholly unseen attack family (Infiltration): test AUC 0.37-0.43 (worse than random), recall <1.5% at every horizon, despite near-perfect in-distribution validation (AUC 0.9999)

requirement_matrix.Scientific confidence: No audited evidence either way; preliminary unaudited evidence points to a real, unresolved risk

requirement_matrix.PS Requirement: Time-series probability score: likelihood of infiltration in the next K time windows
requirement_matrix.Exact/faithful PS interpretation: Reads as a K-indexed (per-step) series, not one whole-horizon scalar

requirement_matrix.Missing work: Add a genuine per-step attack-probability head to the AUDITED VectorWorldModel backbone (see Step 6 / roadmap P1)

candidate_designs_considered.notes: Most defensible option given CIC-IDS-2018's per-day-per-attack-type structure (docs/CIC_IDS2018_DATA_READINESS.md attack timeline: each day/attack-type is largely confined to a specific time window and file). Train on days/windows NOT containing the held-out attack family; test only on windows that DO contain it.

candidate_designs_considered.design: Attack-class holdout (finer than family, e.g. hold out one DoS variant but keep others)
candidate_designs_considered.notes: Also defensible but tests a weaker form of generalization (still seen the broader family); useful as a secondary, easier benchmark.
This is what Phase 3.5-9I already do. It does NOT test attack-family generalization -- it tests whether the model generalizes across time within the same attack types it has seen.

candidate_designs_considered.design: Source-day holdout (hold out an entire day)
candidate_designs_considered.notes: Conflates day-of-capture effects (different attack types happen on different days in CIC-IDS-2018) with attack-family generalization -- less clean than explicit family holdout, but easy to construct and a reasonable secondary check.

candidate_designs_considered.design: Label-family holdout (broad label groupings, e.g. all *BruteForce* labels)
candidate_designs_considered.notes: A pragmatic middle ground between exact-class and whole-day holdout; groups related labels (e.g. FTP-BruteForce + SSH-Bruteforce) as one family.
Explicitly rejected -- violates temporal ordering and would leak flow-adjacency information Phase 3.5's guards exist specifically to prevent.

recommended_protocol.design: Leave-one-attack-family-out, built on top of the EXISTING Phase 3.5 canonical windowed dataset interface (world_model_dataset.py), not a new pipeline
recommended_protocol.train_validation_test_construction: Select ONE attack family present in a clearly bounded time window (e.g. Infiltration, confined to Wednesday-28-02-2018 and Thursday-01-03-2018 per the Phase 2 attack timeline). TRAIN on all windows from the other source days (which contain zero Infiltration-labeled rows). VALIDATE on a held-out slice of the same non-Infiltration days (chronologically, as today). TEST exclusively on windows from the Infiltration day(s).
recommended_protocol.target_definition: Unchanged: future_attack_within_horizon, but now computed with the held-out family's labels only present in the TEST windows
leakage_risks: Must verify NO Infiltration-labeled row appears anywhere in train/validation (a stricter version of the existing split-boundary guard)
Must verify the feature scaler is fit on the NEW train set only (not reuse the old chronological-split scaler)
Must check the held-out day doesn't ALSO contain other, already-seen attack types mixed into the same windows (would partially leak familiarity)
recommended_protocol.metrics: PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, recall at a fixed FPR (reuse choose_threshold_recall_at_fpr from phase6b_ablation.py for consistency with Phase 8A), plus a bootstrap CI given the likely small positive count
recommended_protocol.limitations: CIC-IDS-2018 only has a handful of distinct attack families, each concentrated on 1-2 days -- this limits how many independent held-out-family repeats are possible, and each repeat trains a materially different model (fewer families to learn from), so results should be read as case-study evidence per family, not one aggregate 'generalization score'.

unseen_attack_generalization.can_dataset_support_the_claim: PARTIALLY. The dataset supports building and running the experiment (attack families are cleanly day-bounded per the existing Phase 2 audit), but the SMALL NUMBER of distinct attack families limits how strong or general any resulting claim can be -- a single held-out family (e.g. Infiltration) is a real, useful data point, not proof of generalization to attack types outside CIC-IDS-2018 entirely.

per_step_risk_forecasting.exact_target_needed: For each future step k in 1..6, a binary label current_attack(t+k) (already available per-row in data/windows/*.csv -- this is literally the 'current_attack' field of the future row, already read by world_model_dataset.read_world_model_samples into window_start_sequence/future_attack_step, just not currently exposed as 6 separate per-step training targets).
per_step_risk_forecasting.horizon_windows_complete: Yes for eligible samples -- read_world_model_samples already guards 'index + FORECAST_HORIZON_WINDOWS >= len(rows)' and requires the full t-5..t+6 span to stay inside one split, so every training sample already has 6 complete, real future rows available.
per_step_risk_forecasting.target_leakage_risk: Low if implemented as 6 independent binary heads trained with the existing per-step current_attack(t+k) ground truth (this is exactly what Phase 6B's WorldModelSampleSet.future_attack_step already computes, just collapsed into a single scalar today). Risk would only appear if per-step targets were constructed by re-deriving from PREDICTED states rather than the real logged future rows.
per_step_risk_forecasting.backbone_reusable: Yes -- the existing rollout already produces 6 distinct latent states z(t+1)...z(t+6) (experiments/phase6b_vector_world_model.py: rollout list before mean-pooling). The AttackForecastHead currently DISCARDS this per-step structure by mean-pooling before the final linear layer -- a per-step head would apply the same small MLP to EACH z(t+k) independently instead of the pooled mean.
per_step_risk_forecasting.suitable_losses: BCEWithLogitsLoss per step, summed or averaged across the 6 steps, with a per-step pos_weight computed from TRAIN labels only (mirroring the existing whole-horizon approach)
per_step_risk_forecasting.evaluation_metrics: Per-step PR-AUC/ROC-AUC/F1/recall/FPR (already have per_horizon_state_error and per_horizon_attack_performance as templates in phase6b_vector_world_model.py)
per_step_risk_forecasting.explicit_warning: 1 - P(BENIGN) derived from the MITRE stage head is NOT a substitute for this and must never be presented as native per-step attack probability -- it answers a different question (which stage is most likely) and was fit with a different, stage-classification loss, not an attack/no-attack loss.

approaches_considered.suitability: Strong fit: distribution-free, finite-sample coverage GUARANTEES, and directly wraps the existing trained classifier without retraining or architecture changes

uncertainty_evaluation.primary_recommendation: Conformal prediction. It requires no architecture change, no retraining, trivial compute cost, and directly targets the exact failure mode Phase 8B already documented (naive probability calibration degrading under prevalence shift) with a method that has formal coverage guarantees rather than just empirical hope.
uncertainty_evaluation.fallback_recommendation: Monte Carlo dropout, as a cheap secondary signal (epistemic-uncertainty flag) if conformal prediction's coverage checks fail under the project's specific distribution shift.

representable_interventions_in_157_featu: Suppress/zero traffic-volume-related aggregates for a feature group (approximates 'isolate host' or 'block source' at the STATE level, not the packet level, since raw IP identity is not a feature -- R1)
Reduce port-diversity / rate-related aggregates (approximates 'block destination port' for scan-like behavior)
Reduce specific attack-correlated feature aggregates identified by the explainability output (a direct, feature-space intervention)
not_representable: Literal 'isolate host X' or 'block destination IP Y' -- no endpoint identity exists in the 157-feature state (R1), so host/IP-specific interventions cannot be represented without fabricating identity information that was deliberately excluded
counterfactual_defense.physical_plausibility_concern: Modifying a subset of the 157 standardized features independently can easily produce a state vector that lies outside the manifold of states the StandardScaler/model ever saw during training (e.g. zeroing byte-count aggregates while leaving packet-count aggregates unchanged is not how real traffic behaves) -- the World Model would happily roll forward an unrealistic state without any signal that it left the training distribution.
counterfactual_defense.world_model_rollout_compatible: Yes, mechanically -- LatentTransition is a pure function of the current latent state and can be applied to ANY input state, including a hypothetically edited one. This is precisely why the physical-plausibility concern above matters: mechanical compatibility does not imply the output is meaningful.
counterfactual_defense.simulation_vs_causal_effect_distinction: This must be presented strictly as 'if the observed feature vector had been X instead, the trained model would forecast Y' -- a statement about the MODEL's learned function, not a statement about what would physically happen on the real network if a defender took that action. No causal inference (e.g. do-calculus, actual intervention data) is performed or possible with this setup.
counterfactual_defense.possible_validation: Compare counterfactual-intervention outputs against a real, naturally-occurring state from the dataset that resembles the hypothetical one (nearest-neighbor sanity check) as a weak plausibility signal -- NOT proof of causal validity.
counterfactual_defense.recommendation: SCIENTIFICALLY SAFE ONLY IN A NARROW FORM: (1) restrict interventions to feature-space edits explicitly identified by the explainability output (not arbitrary host/IP actions, which aren't representable anyway), (2) always label the output 'simulated trajectory under a hypothetical feature-state edit', never 'predicted effect of this defensive action', (3) report the nearest-neighbor plausibility check alongside every counterfactual result. If this narrow framing cannot be maintained in the demo UI, DO NOT build this capability -- the broader framing risks a serious, easily-critiqued overclaim.

  -> WORLD MODEL (LatentTransition, recursive x6 rollout) [CURRENT, GREEN]
  -> K-STEP ROLLOUT (z(t+1)...z(t+6)) [CURRENT, GREEN]
  -> PER-STEP ATTACK RISK (new per-step head on existing rollout) [PLANNED, P1]
  -> MITRE STAGE TRAJECTORY (per-step, needs taxonomy fix) [CURRENT + PLANNED FIX, P1]
  -> UNCERTAINTY (conformal prediction wrapper) [PLANNED, P2]

experiment_specifications.hypothesis: The VectorWorldModel architecture, trained without exposure to a given attack family, generalizes poorly to that family at test time (motivated by the preliminary, unaudited zero_shot_results.json signal)
experiment_specifications.dataset: data/windows/*.csv (canonical Phase 3.5 interface), re-split by attack family instead of chronologically within each day
experiment_specifications.split: Train: all windows from source days containing zero examples of the held-out family. Validation: chronological held-out slice of the same train days. Test: all windows from source day(s) containing the held-out family
experiment_specifications.model: VectorWorldModel, identical architecture/hyperparameters to Phase 6B (no architecture search)
experiment_specifications.baseline: The existing Phase 6B chronological-split model, evaluated on the SAME held-out-family test windows for a fair before/after comparison
experiment_specifications.metric: PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, recall at FPR<=5% (choose_threshold_recall_at_fpr, reused unmodified)
experiment_specifications.acceptance_criterion: Documented, reproducible result either way -- a negative result (poor generalization) is an acceptance criterion in itself, per this project's established scientific discipline
experiment_specifications.failure_criterion: N/A -- both outcomes are informative; only a leakage-audit failure would count as an implementation failure
experiment_specifications.leakage_checks: Reuse world_model_dataset.validate_world_model_samples' checks (span-containment, temporal alignment, label recomputation), PLUS a new check confirming zero held-out-family labels appear in train/validation
experiment_specifications.expected_artifact: experiments/results/phaseXX_unseen_attack_generalization/ with metrics.json, leakage-audit report, and comparison against the Phase 6B baseline

experiment_specifications.hypothesis: A per-step head applied independently to each rollout latent z(t+1)...z(t+6) can produce meaningfully differentiated per-step attack probabilities, rather than one pooled whole-horizon number
experiment_specifications.target: 6 independent per-step binary labels: current_attack(t+k) for k=1..6, already derivable from the existing window_start_sequence
experiment_specifications.model: VectorWorldModel backbone (frozen or fine-tuned, to be decided empirically) + a new small per-step MLP head applied to each z(t+k) independently, mirroring AttackForecastHead's existing architecture but without the mean-pool
experiment_specifications.baseline: The existing whole-horizon AttackForecastHead, evaluated against the SAME per-step targets by broadcasting its single prediction to all 6 steps
experiment_specifications.metric: Per-step PR-AUC/ROC-AUC/F1/recall/FPR, compared step-by-step against the broadcast baseline
experiment_specifications.acceptance_criterion: Per-step head achieves materially better per-step metrics than the broadcast baseline, especially at short horizons (t+1, t+2) where more precise timing should be easiest
experiment_specifications.failure_criterion: Per-step head performs no better than the broadcast baseline at any horizon -- would suggest the whole-horizon pooling wasn't actually losing much information
experiment_specifications.leakage_checks: Verify each per-step target uses only that step's real logged current_attack value, never a value derived from the model's own predictions
experiment_specifications.expected_artifact: experiments/results/phaseXX_per_step_risk/ with per-step metrics.json and a direct comparison table against Phase 6B's whole-horizon numbers
